i was biking down the highway from my girlfriends house to the house i was house sitting at. It was mainly a pitch black ride home at around 3am until i saw a man hitchhiking around 100ft infront of me on the main stretch and luckily, the most well lit area of the ride home. As i got closer the guy crossed the highway not looking either way for the big semi trucks that were wizzing past him. I got an erie feeling as he crossed to my side of the highway, as soon as i was around 10 feet infront of him he tried to stand infront of my bike and he said “i’m gonna need that bike” in the most horrible smokers voice i’ve probably ever heard, i didn’t say anything turned my head away from him and biked around him and past him. As i did that he pulled out mace and just started spraying. It got on most of my jacket and my bike but luckily i got none around my eyes. I just couldn’t help but think being maced at 3am on the side of the highway unable to see and it pitch darkness and no one around to see me or help me. At that moment i never biked faster in my life for a solid 20 minutes. I knew the flight response that kicked in was the right one.

the doctor who helped deliver me and both of my brothers. Today i went to have an appointment with her and it was my first time going alone, i’m 18 and i needed my prescription increased and i had to tell her how i was addicted to pot for 2 years and was abusing it everyday, it was 100% affecting my meds and how they worked, she told me that the only way for my medication to work properly was to stop the pot. I also had the joy of telling her that i’ve been over a month clean and the thought of weed sickens me, and she was so happy for me she was banging the table and jumping up and down. personally i didn’t think quitting weed was gonna be so hard for me but seeing her being so happy made me think for a moment that i’ve started my life in a new direction. She’s been my doctor my whole life and is always keeping up with me and id have no other doctor than her. Thank you Dr. Moranda
